terms.comment: “A hollow dish”, on catillus, the small dish or plate.
Classically the bowl in which wine was mixed with water; Andresian’s large bowl. The form crātēr is mostly poetic.

phrases.english: I’ve put a bowl of hot soup in front of you.

phrases.latin: In summō habuimus cāseum mollem … et hēpatia in catillīs
phrases.english: To finish we had soft cheese … and little livers in bowls
Fill the bowl with water; the dog is thirsty.

phrases.latin: Nam plūrimum rēfert aquam nōn esse in eā nisi in ūnō locō quam bibant, eaque mundissima.
phrases.english: For it matters most that there should be water in the yard in one place only, for the hens to drink, and that very clean.

phrases.latin: Vāsa quibus aqua praebētur similia esse dēbent gallīnāriīs, quae colla bibentium admittant
phrases.english: The vessels in which their water is given should be like those for hens, letting in the necks of the birds as they drink

sources: Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: numbered food and kitchen sections
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, pp. 282, 305.
